extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors conducting systematic reviews in optical sensing & communication; IEEE COMST readers and systematic-review practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: A registered PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic survey mapping Optical Integrated Sensing and Communication (O-ISAC) across four optical modalities, producing a unified physical-layer taxonomy, a standardized metric-reporting contract, and structured narrative/quantitative syntheses for IEEE COMST submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA 2020 compliance / registered protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: This work is PRISMA-guided and the repository contains the registered PRISMA protocol. The survey draws on a PRISMA 2020-compliant corpus of 221 peer-reviewed studies (2020–2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register and follow a PRISMA 2020 protocol; archive the registered protocol (DOI/registration) alongside the review so selection and methods are transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database-specific search strings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide database-specific search strings used to identify the corpus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and share the exact queries run against each bibliographic database to ensure reproducibility and allow peers to verify coverage and search sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening and exclusion logs
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain screening and exclusion logs documenting decisions about study inclusion/exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archive schema or logs showing reasons for exclusion at each screening stage to support transparency and allow replication or audit of the selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schema-driven extraction artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use schema-driven extraction artifacts to collect study-level data and metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define structured extraction schemas (fields, units, metadata) and share populated extraction datasets so results and downstream analyses are reproducible and machine-readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: TQAF quality scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply TQAF quality assessment framework (TQAF quality scores) to evaluate included studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score study quality systematically using a recognized assessment framework (here TQAF) and archive the scores and scoring rubric so readers can judge evidence strength and sensitivity to study quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized metric-reporting contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a standardized metric-reporting contract, explicitly separating bandwidth-limited resolution from estimator-dependent accuracy and CRB/FIM bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which metrics to report and how to report them (e.g., clear separation of intrinsic, bandwidth-limited resolution vs estimator-dependent accuracy; include Cramér–Rao bound/Fisher information matrix where appropriate) to reduce heterogeneity and enable fair comparisons across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of metric and scenario heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and document heterogeneity in reported metrics and experimental scenarios which preclude pooled meta-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate compatibility of reported metrics and scenarios before attempting pooling; when heterogeneity is high, refrain from pooled meta-analysis and adopt alternative synthesis methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of synthesis method: narrative and quantitative descriptive analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structured narrative synthesis and quantitative descriptive trade-off analysis instead of pooled meta-analysis when heterogeneity prevents pooling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When pooling is inappropriate, organize findings into structured narratives and perform descriptive quantitative analyses (e.g., trade-off frontiers) to summarize patterns without inappropriate statistical aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corpus scope and inclusion timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and report the corpus scope clearly: peer-reviewed studies from 2020–2025, comprising 221 studies in this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State inclusion criteria (publication types, date ranges, peer-review status) and the final corpus size so readers understand the evidence base and temporal coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage across defined optical modalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Map and cover four optical modalities: fiber (DAS/DFOS), free-space optical (FSO), visible light communication (VLC/LiFi), and photonic-terahertz (photo-THz).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the taxonomy and synthesis explicitly address each targeted modality, documenting modality-specific methods, metrics, and gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified physical-layer taxonomy construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a unified physical-layer taxonomy for O-ISAC that integrates concepts across modalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and present a taxonomy that harmonizes terminology, physical-layer components, and functional roles across modalities to enable cross-domain comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis of rate–range–resolution trade-off frontiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesize rate–range–resolution trade-off frontiers across studies and modalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate and present trade-off analyses (graphical or tabular frontiers) to illustrate performance limits and comparative strengths/weaknesses of modalities and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of cross-domain technology transfer and enabling technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate cross-domain technology transfer opportunities, including enabling technologies such as optical RIS and optical phased arrays (OPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how methods, components, and enabling technologies from one modality could transfer to others, and identify practical barriers and enablers for such transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reproducibility artifacts (data and analysis notebooks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Archive reproducibility artifacts including analysis notebooks, extraction artifacts, and schema-driven data to enable verification and reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release the data, code, and notebooks used for analyses (with clear licenses) so others can reproduce figures, re-run analyses, and adapt methods for follow-up work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency via licensing and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear licensing and metadata (e.g., CC BY 4.0, OSF registration DOI) to enable reuse and citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply an explicit open license and provide persistent identifiers and rich metadata so the review and its artifacts are discoverable, citable, and legally reusable.
